🔊 Pakistan’s army chief departs for Tehran: Source

📌 Tehran, IRNA — Chief of Army Staff of Pakistan, Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, has departed for Tehran to meet with high-ranking Iranian officials, an informed diplomatic source told IRNA.

The source confirmed that Munir left Islamabad moments ago today, which will be his fifth official visit to the Islamic Republic since Pakistan began its mediation efforts to end the joint US–Israeli-imposed war on Iran, earlier this year. Pakistan and Iran have intensified their high-level consultations on mutual interests ever since.
​
During his most recent visit in late August, Pakistan’s army chief met with President Masoud Pezeshkian, Secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council Mohsen Rezaei, Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, and Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni.
​
Last Sunday, Araghchi and his Pakistani counterpart, Mohammad Ishaq Dar, held a telephone conversation to exchange views on bilateral issues and the current regional developments — specifically regarding diplomatic efforts aimed at de-escalating tensions and establishing stability in West Asia.
​
Meanwhile, a Pakistan army spokesperson on Monday emphasized his country’s efforts in maintaining communication channels with all regional actors, including Iran, adding that military escalation in West Asia serves no one’s interests, and that the solution lies solely in diplomacy and negotiations.

🖥 Access to medicine, food, water must not be affected by political disputes: VP

📌 Tehran, IRNA — Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref has called on the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) member states to ensure that access to medicine, water, food, and healthcare services is not affected by political disputes and economic measures.

Addressing a meeting of SCO prime ministers in Tajikistan on Tuesday, Aref said humanitarian considerations must be strengthened in confronting economic warfare, adding that the right to education must also not be sacrificed to political and economic pressure.
​
He cited the deaths of 157 children at a school in Minab during the US-Israeli military aggression against Iran, saying education is a fundamental human right.
​
Aref said the United States and Israel violated international law and international humanitarian law during their February 28 military aggression against Iran.
​
He said the attacks killed the Leader of the Islamic Revolution and schoolchildren on the first day, as well as numerous other innocent civilians, and targeted residential, educational, and medical facilities and infrastructure.
​
He added that Iran’s Armed Forces and united people inflicted a heavy defeat on the aggressors.
​
The Iranian vice president also expressed appreciation for the SCO and its member states for condemning the aggressors and armed attacks, highlighting the need to hold those responsible accountable.
​
Aref also thanked the government and people of Tajikistan for hosting the meeting and praised the SCO secretary-general and his colleagues for facilitating the gathering.
​
He said it was encouraging to see cultural and humanitarian engagement within the organization, underscoring the importance of strengthening cooperation on humanitarian issues.
​
The remarks come amid heightened US military activity in West Asia and increasingly hostile rhetoric by American officials against the Islamic Republic.
​
Tehran has repeatedly warned that US bases and naval assets across the region will be targeted in response to any renewed aggression against Iranian territory.

📡 Trump’s new threat will not break Iranian nation’s resolve: Ambassador

📌 Moscow, IRNA – Iran’s ambassador to the Russian Federation, Kazem Jalali, referring to the US President Donald Trump’s threat of a renewed aggression against the Islamic Republic — specifically the potential use of the so-called “mother of all bombs” — says such threats will not break the resolve of the Iranian nation.

Jalali made the remarks during a specialized event titled “Religion and Power in Iran,” held at the Institute of Scientific Information for Social Sciences of the Russian Academy of Sciences in Moscow, on Monday evening. The occasion also saw the unveiling of a new edition of “State, Religion and Church in Russia and Worldwide,” a quarterly scientific journal dedicated to Iran, as well as the presentation of academic projects by the Ibn Sina Islamic Studies Foundation.
​
During this session — attended by a group of Russian Iranologists, researchers, and students — the ambassador highlighted his country’s resistance and steadfastness against global hegemons, saying the Iranian governance represents a return to human morality, a system where the people resist oppression and refuse to compromise their dignity.
​
Jalali said the Iranian nation’s spirit — and standing as guardians of moral boundaries and human nature — has been visible in the squares and streets since the US-Israeli war of aggression, which he said ensures the threats posed by figures like Trump fail to break the Iranians’ determination.
​
Referring to anti-Iran policies of the US and its allies, he noted that they had applied every available tool at their disposal for nearly five decades to break Iran and the Iranian people, but to no avail because of Iran’s power rooted in innate human nature and morality.
​
He expressed disappointment over the disregard of many global leaders for moral values ​​in their governance, arguing that such a stance leads to atrocities like the Minab school, where American aggressors dropped bombs on Iranian schoolchildren aged seven to twelve.
​
Jalali further said that the absence of morality is the reason some nations legitimatize terrorism and others openly declare their intent to destroy an ancient civilization, a reference to repeated rhetoric of Trump.
​
The atrocities we witness in the world today are the consequence of power devoid of moral substance, a reason behind the Israeli bombardment of innocent and oppressed people in Gaza, resulting in the massacre of over 80,000 human beings, he added.
​
The Iranian Ambassador to Russia also highlighted the shared approaches of the Islamic Republic n and the Russian Federation — specifically their emphasis on national traditions rooted in ethics, and a commitment to justice, peace, and tranquility guided by moral values.

🔊 Putin, Pezeshkian to continue consultations at Moscow gas summit: Iranian envoy

📌 Moscow, IRNA — Iranian ambassador to Russia says consultations between President Masoud Pezeshkian and his Russian counterpart, Vladimir Putin, will continue on the sidelines of the upcoming summit of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) in Moscow, as Tehran and Moscow intensify high-level diplomatic engagement.

In a post on X on Monday, Kazem Jalali positively assessed recent meetings between senior officials of the two countries in Tehran and Dushanbe, Tajikistan, describing their active diplomacy as a sign of their firm determination to shape a new international order.
​
“Active diplomacy at the highest levels is a sign of strategic transformation,” he wrote, pointing to intensive talks between the two countries’ foreign ministers in Tehran, strategic negotiations between their first vice president and prime minister in Dushanbe on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit and continued consultations between their presidents in Moscow.
​
Jalali added that this momentum would pave the way for accelerating the emergence of a multipolar world order.
​
Russian officials have announced preparations for the eighth GECF summit in Moscow, which is scheduled for October 27, with the participation of presidents and senior officials from member countries, including Iran.
​
Preparatory meetings of senior officials and energy ministers are scheduled for October 25–26 ahead of the leaders’ gathering.
